summary: The shared live-water presentation now adds three animated, unequal, skewed upwelling and return-trough cells downstream of each of the three strongest solver-accepted breaking sites. The cells drift independently, use phase-warped shoulders and broken foam rims, and are bounded tightly enough to avoid bullseyes, domes, rails, cards, shoreline seams, and opaque overlays in the matched Zambezi view. This is presentation-only microrelief over the existing analytical rapid, not solved recirculation or measured bathymetry, and it does not establish photoreal whitewater.

implementation.cell_type: overlapping asymmetric elliptical Mexican-hat upwelling and return-trough profiles
implementation.normal_recomputation: limited to the modified presentation neighborhood

zambezi_breaking_water_side.camera_contract: breaking_water_side with an eight-second delay in the same Zambezi run

image_metrics.attribution_caveat: Water, particles, exposure, and background motion continue between frames, so these whole-frame differences are supporting diagnostics rather than exclusive attribution to the boil layer.

zambezi_breaking_water_side.visual_verdict: Retain as a bounded technical candidate. The candidate adds subtle irregular tailwater relief without a concentric bullseye, dome, rail, card, shoreline seam, or opaque overlay. It does not by itself make the analytical rapid or the complete scene photoreal.

remaining_photoreal_defects: The boil cells are bounded procedural presentation cues; they are not calibrated recirculating solver velocity or validated site-specific bathymetry.
The sampled free surface and rapid profile remain smooth and analytical, without a genuinely resolved aerated volume, overturning pile, deep hole, or turbulent eddy field.
Spray is not collision-aware and rock-contact plumes, raft wake, paddle interaction, wet fabric, and camera-lens water remain incomplete or unapproved.

Terrain, banks, geology, ground cover, vegetation, atmosphere, raft equipment, characters, anatomy, PPE, animation, and hand/paddle contact remain below the requested photoreal target in at least one runnable river.
No named guide, geospatial, hydraulic, environment-art, water-VFX, rights, hazard-readability, product, or target-platform reviewer has approved full-scene promotion.
required_external_acceptance_gates: A named whitewater water-VFX and environment-art reviewer must approve the foam, crest, hole, spray, mist, reflection, transmission, and shoreline-contact presentation across representative flow bands.
Qualified guides for the represented rivers must approve rapid identity, aeration placement, line and hazard readability, and raft/swimmer occlusion at the represented flows.
A geospatial or technical-art reviewer must approve source alignment and the labeled procedural terrain, bank, bathymetry, and rapid-geometry infill boundaries.
A rights and provenance reviewer must approve every production texture, mesh, reference-media use, attribution, and redistribution record.
A safety and gameplay-readability reviewer must approve that foam, spray, mist, vegetation, lighting, raft, and characters do not hide hazards, swimmers, rescue targets, or solver failures.
Target-platform qualification must pass desktop performance, memory, streaming, fresh-machine rendering, and required VR or low-power readability budgets.
The product owner must approve the integrated moving-camera river, raft, equipment, character, animation, and water interaction presentation before M9 or photoreal promotion.
